fullDescription:
Three hours fishing in Lan Ha Bay with men who do it for a living.

Lan Ha is the bay next door to Ha Long, off Cat Ba Island, and it is the quieter one. The same drowned karst landscape continues south, but the big cruise fleet mostly stays in Ha Long proper, so Lan Ha has more working boats than tourist ones and around 300 islands with far fewer engines between them.

Fishing here is hand-line and rod work off a small boat rather than anything with a chair and a harness. The fishermen know where the fish sit around the karst bases, which is knowledge you cannot get from a map: the limestone drops steeply into deep water and the productive spots are specific rocks, not general areas.

Floating villages are part of the picture. Families on Lan Ha live on rafts with fish pens underneath, growing grouper and snapper, and the boats work around them.

Three hours is a genuine session rather than a photo opportunity. Catching something is likely but not promised; that is fishing.

This runs from Cat Ba Island, so it fits a stay on Cat Ba rather than a day trip from Hanoi. If you are already on the island for the national park or the climbing, this is the half-day that shows you the water side of it.

We book with Cat Ba Kayak Rental directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers fishing equipment and rods, a local fisherman guide, the boat trip in Lan Ha Bay and the chance to catch local fish.

Three hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Lan Ha Bay: the same karst, far fewer engines
Hand-line and rod fishing off a small working boat
Fishermen who know the specific rocks, not general areas
Floating villages with grouper and snapper pens
Runs from Cat Ba Island, fits a stay rather than a day trip

fullDescription:
A six-hour cruise built for cruise-ship passengers who dock at Ha Long and have one day.

The route covers the three things a first visit should see. Sung Sot, the Surprise Cave, is the largest cave in the bay: two vast chambers reached by a climb from the jetty, lit throughout, with a ceiling high enough that the scale only registers once you are inside. Hang Luon is the opposite kind of cave, a low tunnel through a karst that boats pass through into an enclosed lagoon on the other side. Ti Top Island has the beach and the staircase, around 400 steps to a viewpoint that gives you the classic photograph of the bay spreading out in every direction.

Shore excursion timing is the whole design here. The itinerary is built to get you back to the port with margin, which matters when a ship will not wait, and it is why this runs six hours rather than a leisurely eight.

Lunch is served onboard, entrance fees are included, and the guide works in English throughout.

Worth knowing: the cave and island stops involve real stairs. Sung Sot has a climb to reach it and Ti Top is 400 steps in tropical heat, so this is not a sit-on-deck day.

We book with Up Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers entrance fees, an English-speaking guide onboard, lunch, mineral water, and taxes and service charges.

Six hours from Ha Long port. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Sung Sot, the bay's largest cave, in two vast chambers
Hang Luon, a low tunnel into an enclosed lagoon
Ti Top Island: 400 steps to the classic bay view
Timed to return to port with margin for a ship
Real stairs at both stops, not a deck-chair day

fullDescription:
Four days covering the two UNESCO landscapes of northern Vietnam, with a night on the water and the driving handled.

The route is Hanoi to Ha Long and Lan Ha, then down to Ninh Binh, then back. Both are the same limestone karst doing different things: rising out of the sea in Ha Long, out of rice paddies and a river in Ninh Binh. Seeing them days apart is what makes the comparison land.

Lan Ha is the part that justifies the length. It is the bay south of Ha Long proper, off Cat Ba, where the big cruise fleet does not go. Same drowned karst, around 300 islands, a fraction of the boats. A day trip from Hanoi cannot reach it; an overnight can.

The night is spent on a luxury cruise boat rather than in a hotel, which is the point of an overnight in the bay: the fleet thins out after dark, and morning on the water before the day boats arrive is the quietest the bay ever gets.

Ninh Binh covers Tam Coc by rowing boat through river caves and the climb at Mua Cave, several hundred steps to the ridge.

Limousine transfer between all four legs means reclining seats rather than a coach, which over four days and several hundred kilometres is not a small thing.

We book with SST Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers Hanoi Old Quarter pickup and drop-off, limousine transfers throughout, and one night on a 3, 5 or 6-star luxury cruise depending on the option selected.

Four days. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Both UNESCO karst landscapes: at sea and inland
Lan Ha Bay, which day trips from Hanoi cannot reach
A night on the water, when the fleet thins out
Tam Coc by rowing boat and the Mua Cave ridge climb
Limousine transfers across all four legs

fullDescription:
Two days pairing Ninh Binh with Lan Ha Bay rather than Ha Long, which is a deliberate and better choice.

Lan Ha sits just south of Ha Long proper, off Cat Ba Island. It is the same drowned karst landscape, around 300 islands, but the large cruise fleet concentrates in Ha Long Bay itself, so Lan Ha carries a fraction of the traffic. You get the scenery without the queue of boats in every photograph.

Ninh Binh is the inland version of the same geology. Tam Coc is a two-hour rowing-boat trip through three caves the river runs through, with karst walls close on both sides, rowed by locals who work the oars with their feet. Mua Cave is the climb: several hundred stone steps to a dragon statue on the ridge, and the view that made Ninh Binh famous.

Running it as two days rather than one is what makes each half unhurried. A single day trying to cover both means most of it spent in a vehicle.

All activities and the Tam Coc boat trip are included, along with round-trip air-conditioned transport and a guide throughout. Ninh Binh charges entrance separately at several sites, so having activities covered matters on this route.

We book with Tinny Travel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers pickup and drop-off, round-trip air-conditioned transport, a tour guide, all activities and the Tam Coc boat trip.

Two days. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Lan Ha instead of Ha Long: same karst, far fewer boats
Tam Coc through three river caves, oars worked by foot
Mua Cave: several hundred steps to the ridge dragon
Two days, so neither half is rushed
All activities and the boat trip included

fullDescription:
A night on the bay in a cabin with a window, which is the difference between sleeping on a boat and waking up on one.

The case for an overnight is simple: the day fleet leaves. From late afternoon the bay empties, and the hours after sunset and before the boats return in the morning are the only time Ha Long is quiet. An ocean-view cabin means you see that rather than a corridor wall.

Sung Sot, the Surprise Cave, is the bay's largest: two enormous lit chambers reached by a climb from the jetty, with a ceiling high enough that the scale takes a moment to register. Ti Top Island is the other stop, with a beach and around 400 steps to the viewpoint that produces the classic photograph of karsts running to the horizon.

Cabins come as double, triple or twin share. One practical detail worth knowing in advance: air conditioning on the boat runs on a schedule rather than continuously, typically overnight rather than through the day, which is standard across the Ha Long fleet and not specific to this boat. Days on deck are warm.

An English-speaking guide is aboard throughout.

We book with Sunlighttravel directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers the boat cruise, an English-speaking guide, and a double, triple or twin shared cabin.

Two days, one night. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Overnight, so you see the bay after the day fleet leaves
Ocean-view cabin rather than an inside berth
Sung Sot Cave: two lit chambers, high ceilinged
Ti Top Island and its 400-step viewpoint
Boat air conditioning runs overnight, not all day

fullDescription:
The Hanoi to Ha Long transfer done properly, with a guide, in a limousine van rather than a tourist coach.

The drive is about three and a half hours on the expressway. In a standard sleeper bus or sixteen-seat coach that is an endurance test; in a Vietnamese limousine van, which means eight or nine reclining seats with space between them, it is a comfortable morning.

Having a guide on a transfer is unusual and is what separates this from a seat on a shuttle. The road crosses the Red River delta, flat rice country that turns into the coal hills of Quang Ninh province, and there is a Vietnam in that window that nobody explains to you on a standard bus.

The pearl farm stop is included with its entrance fee. Ha Long's bay waters are used for cultured pearl farming, and the stop shows the seeding and harvesting process. There is a shop attached, as there always is, but the entrance is covered so nothing is required of you.

This is the option to book if you are staying in Ha Long rather than doing a day trip, or if you are joining an overnight cruise and need to arrive at the port rather than return to Hanoi the same night.

We book with Entdecke Travel Vietnam directly, so your place is held with them before your booking is final. The price covers a professional English-speaking guide, air-conditioned transport, a bottle of water per person and the pearl farm entrance fee.

Three and a half hours. Minimum one day's notice.
highlights: Limousine van: eight or nine reclining seats, not a coach
A guide on a transfer, which a shuttle seat does not give
Red River delta rice country into the Quang Ninh coal hills
Pearl farm stop with the entrance fee covered
Made for arriving in Ha Long rather than returning same day
